FireScope – Kerala is an interactive satellite-based wildfire monitoring and analysis platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots.
The project integrates active-fire observations from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS instruments aboard Terra, Aqua, Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 to explore wildfire activity across Kerala, India.
FireScope processes and harmonizes these datasets through geographical filtering, attribute standardization and timestamp preparation. It applies spatial-temporal matching using a mutual nearest-neighbour approach, with exploratory thresholds of 500 metres and 60 minutes, to identify potential relationships between observations from different satellite platforms.
The platform also explores Fire Radiative Power (FRP), matched and unmatched observations, satellite platform distributions, daytime and nighttime activity, and daily and monthly detection trends.
Through an interactive web dashboard, users can explore hotspot locations, filter observations by satellite platform and match status, examine analytical visualizations, and download observation data in CSV format.
Built using Python, FastAPI, Pandas, GeoPandas, JavaScript, Leaflet and Chart.js, FireScope aims to make multi-satellite fire observations more accessible and support comparative analysis of wildfire activity.
The matching results represent potential observation relationships, not confirmed duplicate detections or unique fire incidents.
details:
FireScope – Kerala

FireScope – Kerala is an interactive satellite-based wildfire monitoring and analysis platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, “Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots.”

The project integrates active-fire observations from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS instruments aboard Terra, Aqua, Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 to explore wildfire activity across Kerala, India. It processes the datasets through geographical filtering, attribute standardization and timestamp preparation. A spatial-temporal matching method based on mutual nearest neighbours, using exploratory thresholds of 500 metres and 60 minutes, identifies potential relationships between observations from different satellite platforms.

FireScope provides an interactive dashboard where users can view hotspot locations on a map, explore daily and monthly fire trends, compare satellite platform distributions, examine daytime and nighttime observations, filter records by satellite platform and match status, and download data in CSV format. It also supports analysis of Fire Radiative Power (FRP).

The project aims to make multi-satellite fire observations easier to explore and compare, helping users better understand patterns in wildfire activity and supporting further research and environmental monitoring.

The platform was developed using Python, FastAPI, Pandas, NumPy, GeoPandas, Shapely, SciPy, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet.js and Chart.js.

Its creative approach combines observations from multiple satellite missions into one interactive analytical platform. The team considered geographical accuracy, observation timestamps, spatial distance, time differences, satellite characteristics and clear data visualization. Matching results indicate potential observation relationships, not confirmed duplicate detections or unique fire incidents.
